# Complete canonical cap blocks: a physical second-order rank and stress lemma

This note concerns the fixed-cap volume problem. It gives a necessary
condition at a local volume maximum and a sufficient condition for an
actual improving vertex path. Its compatibility hypothesis is explicit
and strong. It neither classifies general covers nor proves an OC bound.

The exact single-simplex calculation used below is proved in
canonical-simplex-physical-hessian-inertia.md. All cap multipliers here
are nonnegative and the objective multiplier is one.

## 1. Physical setting and the complete-block hypothesis

Fix d>=2 and put m=d+1 and Gamma=(d/m)^d. Select N positive-volume
simplex fibers, with volumes V_z>0, from a finite actual convex fiber
family. All other fibers remain fixed. Assume that an OPEN neighborhood
of the reference labeled vertices of these N simplices is physically
admissible: every choice in that neighborhood realizes exactly the
specified fibers of an actual convex body, with the same integer support
and unchanged other fibers. Thus no active compatibility condition
restricts these vertex directions or accelerations.

Fix finitely many ambient closed halfspaces and their original mixed
cap budgets. An active cap is one whose budget equals its initial mass;
the remaining caps have strict slack. Partition the active caps into
h groups, each containing m caps. At each selected fiber and for each
group, require one of the following two alternatives:

* its m restrictions are precisely the m canonical centroid facet caps
  of that simplex, up to a permutation;
* each restriction is strictly full or strictly empty, with no proper
  restriction.

Strictly full means the whole simplex lies in the open halfspace;
strictly empty means it lies in the open complementary halfspace.
Consequently these trace types persist in a neighborhood. In particular
a group is not allowed to have only part of a canonical tuple proper
on a selected fiber.

Use separate barycentric coordinates on each selected simplex.
A nearby simplex has vertices given by the columns of W_z, with each
column sum one and W_z close to I. These are coordinates for physical
vertex motions, not changes of the ambient caps. The objective M(W)
is the total mixed volume, and C_a(W) is the total mass in cap a.
Both are smooth: a proper trace has the exact rational cut-simplex
formula, a full trace is the simplex volume, and an empty trace is zero.
Contributions of unselected fibers are constant.

We call a cap affected if it has a proper or full trace on some selected
fiber. Active caps that are strictly empty on all selected fibers stay
exactly unchanged and can be omitted from the local inequalities.

## 2. The positive modes and the derivative rank

For each selected fiber choose a vector c_z in R^m with sum c_z=0.
Let A_z have zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries

    (A_z)_ij=(m(c_z)_j+(c_z)_i)/(dm-1),  i!=j,

and let B_z have this off-diagonal part and diagonal -(c_z)_i.
Its column sums vanish. The exact identities are

    tr B_z=0,
    row(B_z)=-dm c_z/(dm-1),
    Q(B_z)=(d^2-1)||c_z||^2/[d(dm-1)].               (1)

Here V_z Q is the physical Hessian of
volume minus (1/(m Gamma)) times the sum of its canonical cap volumes.
These modes form a d-dimensional space at each fiber and a
dN-dimensional direct sum E over the selected fibers.

Every first volume derivative is zero on E. A canonical cap labeled i
has derivative Gamma V_z (row(B_z))_i; a full or empty cap has derivative
zero on E. Therefore the sum of the first derivatives of all m caps
of any one group vanishes on E. The permutations and different V_z
do not alter this identity. If

    L:E -> R^(hm),   L(delta)=(D C_a[delta])_a,

then

    rank L <= dh,    dim ker L >= d(N-h).            (2)

Write K=ker L. Let U be the set of fibers on which EVERY element of
K has zero component. If |U|=u, the du independent coordinate
functionals belonging to those blocks annihilate K. Hence they lie
in the row space of L, and

    |U| <= h.                                       (3)

There is a single delta in K whose components are nonzero at every
fiber outside U: the excluded choices form a finite union of proper
linear subspaces of K. If K={0}, then U consists of all selected fibers
and (3) already gives N<=h; in that case take delta=0.

## 3. All normal first stresses and the full-trace weights

A normal first stress is a vector lambda_a>=0 on affected active caps
such that

    D M = sum_a lambda_a D C_a                       (4)

on all physical vertex directions of the selected simplices.
Set lambda_a=0 on the omitted unaffected caps.
For one selected fiber z, let

    F_z=sum_(a strictly full on z) lambda_a,
    alpha_zi=sum_(a canonical at vertex i on z) lambda_a.

Stationarity in translations of this simplex implies that the
alpha_zi are all equal, say alpha_z. Indeed these translations
produce arbitrary zero-sum row derivatives, and their first volume
derivative is zero. Stationarity in a centroid dilation then gives

    1 = F_z + m Gamma alpha_z.

Consequently

    w_z:=1-F_z=m Gamma alpha_z >=0.                 (5)

The full Lagrangian, restricted to variations of this fiber, is
exactly w_z times its canonical Lagrangian, plus a constant. Thus for
every delta in E,

    D^2(M-sum_a lambda_a C_a)[delta,delta]
       =sum_z w_z V_z Q(delta_z) >=0.                (6)

It is strictly positive precisely when some moved fiber has w_z>0.
Nonnegative multipliers are essential for this last characterization.

Define N_eff(lambda)=#{z:w_z>0}. This counts selected fibers with
some positive proper-cap multiplier. It does not count or remove
their actual source mass. In particular w_z=0 means that this fiber's
first volume derivative is paid entirely by strictly full traces,
not that its volume vanishes.

## 4. Second-order alternative, with the multiplier quantifier retained

Let delta be any member of K. Its first objective and all first active
cap derivatives vanish. Denote the straight-path second derivatives by

    q_0=D^2 M[delta,delta],   q_a=D^2 C_a[delta,delta],

and the first derivative functionals by g_0 and g_a. A physical
acceleration b would give

    M''=q_0+g_0(b),   C_a''=q_a+g_a(b).

There is either an acceleration b satisfying

    q_0+g_0(b)>0,    q_a+g_a(b)<0
                         for every affected active cap a,             (7)

or a normal stress lambda satisfying (4) and

    q_0-sum_a lambda_a q_a <=0.                     (8)

Here is a finite-dimensional proof that also proves normality.
Apply the separating-hyperplane alternative to the affine image
of b in the strict positive orthant given by the left sides of
(7), reversing the cap signs. Failure of (7) gives nonnegative
coefficients (theta,mu_a), not all zero, with

    theta g_0-sum_a mu_a g_a=0,
    theta q_0-sum_a mu_a q_a<=0.

Simultaneously shrink every selected simplex about its own centroid.
This is an allowed first direction by the open-neighborhood assumption.
Every affected cap has strictly negative derivative: each proper
canonical trace scales with the simplex, as does a full trace.
Thus theta=0 would contradict the first displayed equality evaluated
on this shrinking direction. Hence theta>0 and lambda_a=mu_a/theta
gives (4) and (8). If no cap is affected, an objective-increasing
acceleration exists directly and there is no exceptional case.

If (7) holds, the actual path

    W_z(t)=I+t(delta_z)+(t^2/2)b_z

has larger total volume and smaller masses in every affected active
cap for all sufficiently small positive t. The open admissibility
hypothesis preserves convex compatibility, all original fiber
identities and all trace types. Unaffected active caps stay identical,
and inactive caps remain within their original budgets by continuity.
This is an actual fixed-budget improvement, not only a positive
quadratic form on a formal tangent space.

## 5. Consequences for a local maximum

At a local fixed-cap volume maximum (7) is impossible. Choose delta
nonzero on every block outside U as in Section 2. Equations (6) and
(8) force w_z=0 on every such block. We have therefore proved:

    At a local maximum there exists a normal stress whose positive
    proper-cap fibers among the selected fibers are contained in U.
    In particular, N_eff(lambda)<=|U|<=h.           (9)

This is an existence statement for one stress. A different first
stress may have a larger effective support.

Two useful sufficient conditions for a physical improving path follow.

1. If EVERY normal first stress has N_eff>h, then (9) is impossible,
   and the acceleration alternative produces an improvement.
2. If no active cap is strictly full on a selected fiber, (5) gives
   w_z=1 for every normal first stress and every selected fiber.
   Consequently N>h forces an improvement.

The second condition holds in particular if every selected fiber has
volume greater than every active cap budget. That comparison is only
a sufficient way to exclude full traces; it is not part of the main
rank or stress identity.

The count agrees with both basic calibrations. One complete canonical
group shared by N>=2 free simplices has no full traces and gives an
improvement. With one independently localized canonical group per
fiber, h=N, its positive-mode derivative map has zero kernel. Thus
the count does not contradict the strict constrained stability of
the separately localized planar example.

There is no need to assume surjectivity of all hm cap derivatives.
Conversely, finding ONE normal stress with N_eff>h is insufficient
for the acceleration argument. The separating stress in (8) can be
different. Even in a two-variable smooth problem this distinction
matters: maximize x subject to x<=0 and x-y^2<=0 at (0,0).
The point is a global maximum and the direction (0,1) is critical.
The stress on the second constraint alone gives the positive
Lagrangian Hessian 2 in that direction, whereas the stress on the
first constraint gives zero. This example is solely a multiplier
quantifier calibration, not an actual convex-fiber counterexample.

## 6. Why partial canonical tuples do not have the same rank bound

The complete-tuple hypothesis cannot be replaced by “every proper
trace is canonical.” Here is an actual two-fiber rank calibration in
d=2. At bases z=0,1 take the same barycentric triangle
lambda_0+lambda_1+lambda_2=1, lambda_i>=0. Fix three ambient caps

    lambda_0 >= 1/3-4z/3,
    lambda_1 >= 1/3-4z/3,
    lambda_2 >= -1+4z/3.

At base zero the first two are canonical and the third is strictly
full. At base one the first two are strictly full and the third is
canonical. These three caps cover each entire fiber space, and the
convex hull of the two triangles is an actual full-dimensional body
with exactly the displayed integer fibers.

On the positive modes the first fiber contributes arbitrary derivatives
in rows 0 and 1 and zero in row 2; its remaining row derivative is
free to make their local canonical sum zero. The second fiber
contributes an arbitrary row 2 derivative and zero in rows 0 and 1.
The three-row derivative map therefore has rank 3, which exceeds d=2.
No claim that this calibration is a critical-cover maximizer is made.

## 7. Scope

The lemma allows different simplex shapes, volumes and vertex
permutations, all expressed in their own physical barycentric charts.
It retains all full-trace volume terms and all original cap budgets.
It does not remove active compatibility constraints, supporting
degeneracies, partial canonical incidences, or general nonsimplex
fibers. An application to a fixed critical cover additionally needs
that its coverage property persists on the admissible family; for
example this is automatic for a fixed cover of all relevant fiber
spaces. Neither the rank count nor (9) is an arbitrary-cover
classification or a global depth bound.

The companion ../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_aligned_canonical_cap_blocks.py passes 114 exact
checks of the positive lifts, complete-group ranks, forced-zero blocks,
full-trace weights, actual partial-group rank calibration and multiplier
quantifier example. Separation and the arbitrary-dimensional statements
are proved above rather than inferred from the finite checks.
